intelligence.essence: Every orb carries two gear rings: the outer and the inner. Both visible. The inner ones noticeable, the outer ones present. And they rotate against each other — one going forward, one going back — like a real machine.
intelligence.human_view:
The orbs had lost their outer gears in a revision, and the inner gears had faded to near-invisible. Shawn caught it on sight: bring the outside ones back, make the inside ones more noticeable, and set them turning in opposite directions. A machine where every part moves the same way looks dead; counter-rotation is what makes it feel alive.

"You should make the inside ones more noticeable and you should make the outside ones come back and one should be going forward one should be going back."
intelligence.simple_view: Each round orb has two rings of little gear teeth, one inside and one outside, and they turn in opposite directions — one this way, one that way — like a real machine working. That's what makes it feel alive.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, you know how a real clock's wheels turn against each other, one clockwise and one the other way? The little dials are made like that — two rings of teeth, both easy to see, turning against each other. A picture of a machine sits still; a real machine moves.
intelligence.naya_view: Every orb I ship carries both gear rings — outer restored, inner noticeable — counter-rotating. Motion is meaning: the eye reads 'living' before it reads any number. Any future moving part inherits this: visible, noticeable, turning against its neighbor.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the ALIVE law at its smallest scale: touch equals movement, nothing static, nothing flat. The counter-rotating gears are the difference between a picture of a machine and the machine itself — the Real Object Law in motion. When the eye catches two rings turning against each other, the brain reads "living" before it reads anything else.
